answer: An agent marketplace can require every account to lock a refundable stake before its bids count, then slash part of that stake when evidence proves identities coordinated as one operator. Each Sybil identity therefore ties up capital and risks a real loss; the saffron market should price admission above the expected reward per account, so adding many accounts costs more than it earns. A marble token can mark each locked stake, while a public river of bids lets auditors spot duplicate behavior and trigger a fair appeal before slashing.
